traits.note: Abrams (vol. 1, 1923, p. 50), Taxaceae: evergreen trees or shrubs with linear leaves set in a spiral that mostly look two-ranked, the flattened leaf base twisting them into one plane; the sexes on separate plants.

traits.phyllotaxis_pattern.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 158, family Taxaceae: phyllotaxis pattern spiral, often twisted so it looks 2-ranked, to decussate, usually; read as {"spiral": "often", "decussate": "often"}.

traits.leaf_habit.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 158, family Taxaceae: leaf habit evergreen; read as "evergreen".

traits.leaf_arrangement.note: Wikipedia, Taxaceae (read 2026-10-16): leaves spirally set, often twisted at the base so they look two-ranked; opposite in Amentotaxus (our addition).
